headline: Embedding validity checks into LLM and agent workflows for biological data analysis
label: Computational Biology Workflow Tools
summary: Recent preprints place assumption and identifiability checks inside LLM-assisted workflows, constraining which conclusions a pipeline can reach.
synthesis: The common thread is a validity condition encoded directly into the step that produces a result, rather than a new core algorithm. DE-Rigor-Agent gates the choice among six bulk RNA-seq differential expression methods on assumption compatibility before execution. The epidemic ODE study benchmarks whether LLMs can classify parameter-level structural identifiability, with top accuracy near 88%. The ECS framework applies related calibration logic to LLM line-of-therapy adjudication, reporting 5% residual error with 44.6% of cases reviewed in myeloma simulations. These items differ in domain and data type, and only the first two directly test assumption or identifiability conditions; the third addresses error calibration through human-in-the-loop selection. What is new is placement: the check constrains which outputs a workflow can produce.
